proposals.evidence: The kāṭ-/kaṭ- verb belongs to Turner kartati cuts. Platts s.v. kāṭnā independently attests biting as an ordinary sense of the same verb. These are unaccompanied inflected forms, or an imperative/past pair of that verb; no take/give/eat auxiliary is present.

proposals.evidence: The complete compound has cut/bite + take. Platts records kāṭ-lenā bite off; Turner 10948 explicitly includes the take paradigm le-, Old Awadhi līnha, Old Marwari liyo and Gujarati līdhũ. Both ordered lexical constituents are saved, retaining local past/person endings.
